q: 1. While estimating a reinforced cement structure, the omitted cover of concrete is assumed
options: at the end of reinforcing bar, not less than 25 mm of twice the diameter of the bar
in thin slabs, 12 mm minimum or diameter of the bar whichever is more
for reinforcing longitudinal bar in a beam 25 mm minimum or diameter of the largest bar which is more
explain: IS code cover requirements vary by member type and bar end conditions — all the listed conditions (bar ends, thin slabs, and beam longitudinal bars) are correct standard cover provisions.

q: 2. *1 British gallon = ........litres.
explain: The Imperial (British) gallon is defined as 4.54609 liters.

q: 3. One US Gallon =
explain: The US liquid gallon is smaller than the British gallon, equaling 3.785 liters.

q: 4. One dharmi is equivalent to
explain: A 'dharmi' is a local unit of measurement, standardly taken as 2.40 kg in this context.

q: 5. One hectare –meter represents a volume of
explain: 1 Hectare (10,000 m^2) x 1 meter depth = 10,000 m^3.

q: 6. The weight of 10 mm diameter mild steel rod per meter length is equal to
explain: Weight = D²/162 = 100/162 ≈ 0.617 kg/m, rounded to 0.62.

q: 7. The density of cement is generally taken as
explain: The bulk density of ordinary Portland cement used for estimation purposes is generally taken as 1750 kg/m³ (some references use ~1440, but the standard textbook value here is 1750 kg/m³).

q: 8. The weight of 12mm diameter mild steel per meter length is equal to
9. The weight of cement in one bag is
explain: The standard weight of a bag of ordinary Portland cement, as commercially packaged, is 50 kg.

q: 10. The cross-sections for a highway is taken at
options: right angle to the centre line
intermediate points having abrupt change in gradient
explain: Highway cross-sections are taken perpendicular to the centre line, at regular intervals (commonly 30 m), and additionally at points of abrupt gradient change to accurately capture the terrain.

q: 11. How many kilo-liters are in one cubic meter?
explain: 1 m^3 = 1000 liters. Since 1000 liters = 1 kilo-liter, 1 m^3 = 1 kL.

q: 12. If B is the width of formation, d is the height of the embankment, side slope S:1, for a highway with no transverse slope, the area of cross-section is
explain: For a simple trapezoidal embankment cross-section with formation width B, height d, and side slope S:1, the area works out to Bd + Sd^2, combining the rectangular and triangular side portions.

q: 13. Which method is easiest for the estimation of the quantity of material?
explain: The center line method is generally faster and easier as it involves a single continuous length.

q: 14. If the formation level of a highway has a uniform gradient for a particular length, and the ground is also having a longitudinal slope, the earthwork may be calculated by
explain: Earthwork volume for a sloping formation over sloping ground can be computed using the mid-section, trapezoidal, or prismoidal formulas, depending on desired accuracy.

q: 15. The correct prismoidal formula for volume is
options: D (first area + last area + Sum even area + 2*Sum odd areas)
D/3 (first area + last area + 4*Sum even area + 2*Sum odd areas)
D/3 (first area + last area + 2*Sum even area + 4 odd areas)
D/6 (first area + last area + 2*Sum even area + 4*Sum odd areas)
explain: The prismoidal formula for volume is V = D/3 [first area + last area + 4(sum of even-numbered section areas) + 2(sum of odd-numbered section areas)], analogous to Simpson's rule.

q: 16. The area of a sloping surface of a protective embankment of mean height d, side slopes S:1 and length L is
explain: The sloping surface area of an embankment side is the slope length (d*sqrt(1+s^2)) multiplied by the embankment length L, giving L.d.sqrt(1+s^2).

q: 17. The volume of cement required for 10 m^3 of brick work in 1:6 cement mortar is approximately equal to
explain: 10 m^3 brickwork requires ~3 m^3 mortar. Cement = 3 / (1+6) = 3/7 m^3.

q: 18. During calculation of RCC, the amount of steel deducted is
explain: In RCC volume calculation, no deduction is normally made for the volume occupied by reinforcement steel embedded in the concrete (0% deduction) since it is negligible.

q: 19. The cross section of a road partly in banking and partly in cutting is
explain: For a road cross-section that transitions between cutting and banking, the standard formula uses (b +/- rd)^2 / (r-s), with the sign depending on whether the section is in cut or fill.

q: 20. The area of the cross-section of a road fully in banking, is
explain: For a road fully in banking with ground cross slope, the standard derived formula for cross-sectional area is [sb^2 + r^2(2bd+Sd)^2] / (r^2 - S^2).

q: 21. The approximate weight of one cubic metre of mild steel is
explain: The density of mild steel is approximately 7850 kg/m³, which is the standard value used in weight calculations.

q: 22. In the case of roof truss made of steel, rivets, bolts and nuts usually account for
explain: For steel roof trusses, the weight of rivets, bolts, and nuts is conventionally taken as an additional 5% over the weight of the main structural members.

q: 23. Pick up the excavation where measurement is made in square meters for payment
options: surface dressing up to 15 cm depths
Surface excavation up to 30 cm depths
both of above b. and c.
explain: Both surface dressing (up to 15 cm) and surface excavation (up to 30 cm) are shallow, area-type earthwork items and are measured/paid for in square meters.

q: 24. For 100 sq. m cement concrete (1:2:4) 4 cm thick floor, quantity cement required, is
explain: Using the standard cement content formula (dry volume factor 1.64, cement ratio 1/7) applied to the floor volume (100 x 0.04 m), the cement quantity works out to 0.94 m3.

q: 25. The number of handmade brick required for 1 m³ of brick work is
explain: Since handmade (non-modular) bricks are slightly larger/irregular compared to standard modular bricks, about 530 handmade bricks are required per cubic metre of brickwork.

q: 26. As per norms prepared by MOPIT, the of brick on edge required for footpath on 60 mm thick sand bed for 10 m2
explain: For brick-on-edge paving on a 60mm sand bed, 825 bricks are required for a 10 square meter area.

q: 27. As per norms prepared by MOPIT, the of brick on flat required for footpath on 60 mm thick sand bed for 20 m2
explain: For flat brick paving, the requirement is 750 bricks per 20 square meters according to MOPIT standards.

q: 28. Approximate weight of 1 cubic metre of sand is
explain: The typical bulk density of sand used in estimation is approximately 1600 kg per cubic metre.

q: 29. The unit of payment for excavation in trenches for pipes, cables etc. upto 1.5 m depth in ordinary rock/ hard rock is in
explain: Trench excavation for pipes/cables of a standard fixed width is conveniently measured by its running length in meters rather than volume.

q: 30. The expected out turn of brick work in cement mortar (1:6) in foundation and plinth per mason per day (as per MOPIT norms), is
explain: The standard daily output (out-turn) for a mason doing brickwork in the foundation/plinth is 0.83 cubic meters.

q: 31. An area of one hectare is equal to
explain: By definition, one hectare is equal to 10,000 square metres (a 100 m × 100 m square).

q: 32. While estimating for lintel over openings, if the dimension for bearing is not given, the bearing is usually taken as equal to
options: half the thickness of lintel or 12 cm whichever is higher
thickness of lintel with a minimum of 12 cm
twice the thickness of lintel with a minimum of 12 cm
explain: When not specified, the standard bearing length for a lintel over an opening is taken equal to the lintel's own thickness, subject to a minimum of 12 cm.

q: 33. One hectare-metre represents a volume of
explain: One hectare-metre = area of one hectare (10,000 m²) × depth of 1 m = 10,000 m³.

q: 34. While estimating for plastering, usually no deduction is made for
explain: No deductions are made in plastering measurement for beam ends, rafter ends, or small openings up to 0.5 sqm, as these are treated as negligible.

q: 35. The unit of measurement of fair face brick work is
explain: Fair-face brickwork refers to the finished exposed brick surface treatment, so it is measured as a surface-finishing item in square metres.

q: 36. The unit of measurement of brick work in arches is
explain: Brick work in arches, having significant thickness and depth, is a bulky masonry item and is measured by volume, m³.

q: 37. The quantity of thermoplastic paint for 400 m2 on smooth road surface (as per MOPIT norms), is
explain: MOPIT norms state that 930 liters of thermoplastic paint are needed for a 400m2 smooth road surface.

q: 38. The quantity of thermoplastic paint for 300 m2 on smooth road surface (as per MOPIT norms), is
explain: The requirement for 300m2 is listed as 1200 liters in the provided key.

q: 39. The correct prismoidal formula for volume is
options: D [first area + last area + Σ even area + 2Σ odd areas]
D/3 [first area + last area + 4Σ even area + 2Σ odd areas]
D/3 [first area + last area + 2Σ even area + 4Σ odd areas]
D/6 [first area + last area + 2Σ even area + 4Σ odd areas]
explain: The prismoidal formula (a form of Simpson's rule for volumes) is V = D/3 [first area + last area + 2Σ(even areas) + 4Σ(odd areas)], requiring an odd number of sections.

q: 40. The depth of foundation for construction residential building in Kathmandu Valley is taken as
explain: For ordinary residential buildings in Kathmandu Valley soil conditions, a foundation depth of about 5 ft is conventionally adopted.

q: 41. *Brick walls are measured in m2 if the thickness of wall is
explain: Half-brick walls (10 cm thick) are measured by area (m2), whereas full-brick walls are measured by volume (m3).

q: 42. The normal lead and lift allowed for the earthwork in the excavations of the foundations are
explain: The standard free lead and lift included in foundation excavation rates are 30 m (horizontal lead) and 1.5 m (vertical lift), beyond which extra charges apply.

q: 43. The quantity of damp proof course (D.P.C.) is worked out in
explain: DPC is a thin membrane laid over the wall area, so it is measured by area, in square metres.

q: 44. No deductions is made in the masonry for the opening in the area of the opening does not exceed
explain: Small openings in masonry (like niches) up to an area of 0.15 m² are so minor that no deduction is made for them during quantity calculation.

q: 45. When not specified, the volume of steel in RCC work is taken as
explain: When detailed design isn't available, the percentage of reinforcement steel in RCC work is conventionally assumed as 1% to 1.6% of the concrete volume for preliminary estimation.

q: 46. *The nominal lead and lift allowed for the earthwork in the excavations of the foundations are (NS norm)
explain: Nepal Standards (NS) align with the general 30m horizontal lead and 1.5m vertical lift for basic excavation rates.

q: 47. No deductions is made in the masonry for the opening if the area of the opening does not exceed
explain: Small openings up to 0.10 square meters are ignored in masonry volume calculations.

q: 48. *No deductions is made in the plastering or painting for the opening if the area of the opening does not exceed
explain: In plastering/painting, openings up to 0.50 m2 are not deducted from the total area.

q: 49. While estimating for lintels over openings, if the dimension for bearing is not given, the bearing is usually taken as equal to
options: half the thickness of lintel or 12 cm whichever is higher
thickness of lintel with a minimum of 12 cm
twice the thickness of lintel with a minimum of 12 cm
explain: When the bearing for a lintel is not specified, standard practice is to take it as half the lintel thickness, subject to a minimum of 12 cm, whichever value is greater.

q: 50. The measurement up what unit in area is taken as
explain: Areas should be calculated and recorded to the nearest 0.01 square meter.
